A good way to warm up into a stretch to get to your feet is to stand, feet just less than shoulder width apart (enough that you will be able to touch your feet without twisting to the side). Then tuck your chin to your chest, and slowly, and gently start to bring your head and shoulders down as if you are trying to touch the crown of your head to the floor, gently rolling (curling) your back and easing into a front bending at your waist. Let your arms act as dead weights that will drift the upper half of your body slowly forward. Once your fingers are just grazing above your toes, hang in that position for a few seconds. You'll feel your butt, back of knees and your sides start to stretch a bit. Keep holding. After a few more seconds your fingers won't be grazing your feet, they'll be on them. Hold for a few more seconds, then, starting with your waist, start to bring yourself back into a standing position, uncurling in the same order (waist, back, shoulders, neck). Once standing, very gently bring your head back to look up, and curl the top of your back and rotate the shoulders aback a bit too (so Iike bring your upper body back by about 30-35') so that you are looking at the ceiling. Elongate your neck a bit, with your chin up. Hold for 5 seconds. Repeat 2-3 times to whole process for the first 4-5 days. After a week of this when you are leaning forward, hands towards your feet, you might be able to actually clasp your ankles and do some pulse stretches (your breasts will be saying 'hello!' To your knees!). You'll also be able to curl your fingers OVER your toes. (I can get my hands into the arch of my foot now if I stretch in a sitting down position with my legs in a v!) Do the stretch slowly and gently though.

You're welcome :) Is this in relation to any stretches I mentioned or just generally? If in general, try warming up with gentle rotations first. Standing erect, feet just less than shoulder width apart, and back and neck aligned, keep your arm straight, and hand tilted as if you are doing the breast stroke. But don't tense up your body (you will fuck your neck up if you do)

Focusing on one side first, slowly bring the arm forward in a clockwise movement, gently, with your hand still straight and tilted so it's almost doing a slicing motion through the air. After 20 clockwise rotations, do 20 counter clockwise ones, and then 15 clockwise ones. Immediately after, gently shake your arm a bit to ease up the muscles before swinging said arm up and across your chest so your forearm is over your opposite shoulder (I.e, if you rotated with the right arm, did the shake and then swing, the forearm with be over your left shoulder). After a few gentle pulses, position your arm up and back onto its correct side, but behind your neck (so your right elbow is pointing at the ceiling, but the right hand downwards, the back of your hand on your spine in between your shoulderblades), if you can, try to push the elbow down a bit so increase the stretch (if it really hurts, stop immediately. I am not a doctor and I don't want you injured!)

Shake again.

Repeat same action with other arm (rotations, backwards rotations, forward rotations, shake, stretch, super stretch, shake). Shoulder help significantly.

If you want something more static but intense, but that will hurt more, look for a pull up bar in your gym and place your hands on it so the knuckles are facing the ceiling. Gently kneel forward to apply pressure on your shoulders. Slowly and steadily. Keep leaning and hanging so you are kneeling down. If strong enough, hoist your body a bit, lift your legs up behind you (your feet just skimming or touching your butt) and hang for a few seconds. Be relaxed, not tensed! Repeat for 10 seconds and give yourself a 20 second break before doing another few hangs. Again, gently shake it off after, otherwise your arms will hate you

It will hugely improve the flexibility in your arms and shoulders (and neck)
